record.paper_title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let D*_n be the maximum leaf height of CTCS(n), the continuous-time critical beta-splitting tree on n leaves. Prove that D*_n / log n converges in probability to a constant c, and determine that constant.

evidence.quote: Write D∗_n for the height of the random tree CTCS(n) itself, that is the maximum leaf height.
Open Problem 3 Show that D∗_n ∼ c log n in probability, and identify the constant c.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the continuous-time critical beta-splitting tree CTCS(n) on n leaves as follows. For each integer m ≥ 2, let q(n,i) := (n/i(n-i)) / H_{n-1} for 1 ≤ i ≤ n-1, where H_{n-1} = sum_{j=1}^{n-1} 1/j; this is a probability distribution on {1,...,n-1} (it is symmetric: q(n,i)=q(n,n-i)). Starting with a single block of size n, recursively split each block of size m ≥ 2 into two blocks of sizes (i, m-i) with probability q(m,i), independently across blocks. Assign to each block of size m an independent exponential holding time with rate 1/(m-1) (equivalently, the time between successive splits at a node corresponding to a block of size m is Exponential(1/(m-1))); blocks of size 1 (leaves) do not split. This yields a continuous-time rooted binary tree with n leaves, where the height of a leaf is the total elapsed time from the root to that leaf.

Let D*_n denote the maximum leaf height of CTCS(n), i.e. the height of the deepest leaf.

Prove that there exists a constant c ∈ (0, ∞) such that
   D*_n / log n  →  c   in probability  as  n → ∞,
and identify the value of c.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. The companion paper on heights establishes only tail bounds showing P(D*_n ≥ (2+ε) log n) ≤ n^(-ρε) for some ρ > 0, and explicitly states convergence of D*_n/log n to a constant as a conjecture. Subsequent works (including the 2024 contraction paper and the 2025 CLT paper) address the height of a uniformly random leaf D_n (proving D_n/log n → 1/ζ(2) = 6/π^2 in probability with a CLT), but do not resolve the maximum leaf height question.

status_evidence.title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree: Heights and Related Results
status_evidence.snippet: There exists ρ>0 such that for all ε∈(0,1) we have ℙ(𝒟_n ≥ (2+ε) log n) ≤ 1/n^(ρε). ... We conjecture that both 𝒟_n/log n and ℒ_n/log² n converge, in probability, to constants.
status_evidence.claim: Only tail bounds are proven; convergence of D*_n/log n is stated as a conjecture, not a theorem.

status_evidence.title: Some central limit theorems for critical beta-splitting trees
status_evidence.snippet: The paper studies the height D_n of a uniformly random leaf and proves a CLT around (ζ(2))^{-1} log n; it does not address the maximum leaf height.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) follow-up work addresses random-leaf heights, not the maximum, indicating the maximum-height question is still open.
